head: e5245d08d2fe5c05f67742fd8ec5a67b759ca316
notes: bootstrap.go and profilesettings.go are brand-new files in this range; repos.go/routines.go/repos_test.go/routines_test.go are modified. Reviewed against context/rules/go.md (read in full, this session). Cross-chunk: handleProfileSave's bare pass-through of s.presentation.saveProfileSelection's error (profilesettings.go:89) could not be judged against RULE-GOLANG-ERR-001's 'already fully contextualized callee' exception because the presentation package lives outside this chunk — flagged here only as a note, not a finding.

findings.fix: Rename new booleans to read as predicates: bootstrapRun.running -> isRunning (bootstrap.go:26, and its 4 other uses in the file), repos.go's cached/data.Cached -> isCached, refresh -> ... (refresh is already a predicate-shaped read, keep), profilesettings.go's audienceChanged -> isAudienceChanged.
findings.claim: RULE-GOLANG-BOOL-001 requires booleans to read as predicates (isX/hasX/shouldX). This diff introduces several new booleans that do not: bootstrapRun.running (bootstrap.go:26, plus reads at lines 47,102,109,125,129,138,140), worktreeStatusPage.Cached and the local `cached` (repos.go:356-357,419), and handleProfileSave's `audienceChanged` (profilesettings.go:88,96).
findings.evidence: Re-read bootstrap.go:23-28 (bootstrapRun struct: `mu sync.Mutex; pid int; running bool; startedAt time.Time`) and its uses at 47/102/109/125/129/138/140 in the committed file (git show e5245d08d2fe5c05f67742fd8ec5a67b759ca316) — none of these are pre-existing (bootstrap.go is a wholly new file, confirmed via `git diff --stat` showing 197 insertions/0 deletions). Re-read repos.go:356-357 and 419 (git show, committed) — `cached` and `Cached` are new names introduced by this diff (confirmed via `git diff` hunk showing these lines as additions, replacing the old Base/Kind/Query fields). Re-read profilesettings.go:88,96 (git show, committed; profilesettings.go is a wholly new file, 253 insertions/0 deletions) — `audienceChanged` is new. All four names fail the isX/hasX/shouldX predicate-naming rule, and the pattern recurs across every one of the new/changed files in this chunk, so it clears the 'codebase is full of them -> legacy' exemption only in the sense that it's a new, repeated pattern this diff itself introduces, not inherited legacy.

findings.fix: Drop the bare `// since` / `// extra-prompt` comments in bootstrapEnv (bootstrap.go:179,188) and the bare `// audience` / `// language` comments in handleProfileSave (profilesettings.go:71,78) — RULE-GOLANG-COMMENT-002 sanctions this field-labeling comment style only inside tests and Validate() methods; neither bootstrapEnv nor handleProfileSave is either.
findings.claim: RULE-GOLANG-COMMENT-002 restricts grouping/field-label comments to tests and Validate() methods. This diff's two new files each add that exact comment shape (a bare `// <field>` line directly above the check for that field) in plain handler/helper functions: bootstrapEnv (bootstrap.go:179 `// since`, 188 `// extra-prompt`) and handleProfileSave (profilesettings.go:71 `// audience`, 78 `// language`). Neither function is a Validate() method or a test.
findings.evidence: Re-read bootstrap.go:176-197 (committed, git show) — bootstrapEnv is a free function building env strings from form values, not a Validate() method. Re-read profilesettings.go:65-111 (committed, git show) — handleProfileSave is an http.HandlerFunc-shaped method, not a Validate() method. Both comments restate the identifier that follows (`// since` above `since = strings.TrimSpace(since)`) with no non-obvious content, which is exactly what RULE-GOLANG-COMMENT-001/002 reserve for the Validate()/test shape (RULE-GOLANG-VALIDATE-002's own example uses identical syntax: `// GameId` above a field check) — applying it outside that sanctioned location is the violation.

findings.fix: Move the `statuses := []repos.WorktreeStatus{test.status}` wrapping into the case literal (e.g. store `statuses []repos.WorktreeStatus` as a testCase field, set once per append block) so the t.Run body is flat: `assert.Equal(t, test._expectedId, worktreeSessions(test.statuses, test.index)[test.status.Worktree].Id)`.
findings.claim: TestWorktreeSessionsPrefersBranchOverRecycledDir's t.Run body (repos_test.go:286-290) contains two `:=` declarations (`statuses`, `sessions`) before the final assert, violating RULE-GOLANG-TEST-008's 'completely flat: value / assert / assert — zero declarations' requirement for the loop body.
findings.evidence: Re-read repos_test.go:285-291 (committed, git show e5245d08d2fe5c05f67742fd8ec5a67b759ca316): `for _, test := range tests { t.Run(test._id, func(t *testing.T) { statuses := []repos.WorktreeStatus{test.status}; sessions := worktreeSessions(statuses, test.index); assert.Equal(t, test._expectedId, sessions[test.status.Worktree].Id) }) }` — two declarations precede the single assertion, matching the rule's own counter-example shape ('zero declarations, no if, no early return') rather than the sanctioned 'value / assert / assert' flat body. This is new code (the whole test function was added by this diff, confirmed in the repos_test.go diff hunk).

findings.fix: Wrap the os.CreateTemp error with context before handing it to respond.WithInternalServerError, matching the sibling cmd.Start() handling a few lines below: `respond.WithInternalServerError(fmt.Errorf("handleWelcomeBootstrap: Failed to create bootstrap log file: %w", err), w)`.
findings.claim: handleWelcomeBootstrap passes the os.CreateTemp error to respond.WithInternalServerError bare (bootstrap.go:71-75), with no Component.Method context, while the same function wraps the cmd.Start() error with `fmt.Errorf("handleWelcomeBootstrap: Failed to start claude: %w", err)` nine lines later (bootstrap.go:97) — an inconsistent application of RULE-GOLANG-ERR-001 within one function.
findings.evidence: Re-read bootstrap.go:71-98 (committed, git show) side by side: line 71-75 `logFile, err := os.CreateTemp(...); if err != nil { respond.WithInternalServerError(err, w); return }` versus line 94-98 `if err := cmd.Start(); err != nil { ...; respond.WithInternalServerError(fmt.Errorf("handleWelcomeBootstrap: Failed to start claude: %w", err), w); return }`. os.CreateTemp's error is a bare stdlib path error with no indication of which operation failed, so it is not 'already fully contextualized' — the sanctioned bare-pass-through exception in RULE-GOLANG-ERR-001 does not cover it, unlike cases where the callee is a first-party function that already prefixes its own errors (which I could not verify for the profilesettings.go instances since the presentation package is outside this chunk, so those are left as a cross-chunk note rather than a finding).
